name: Palace Hotel, San Francisco
insider_take: This storied Palace Hotel has been the crown jewel of San Francisco hospitality since 1875, surviving earthquakes and hosting presidents in its opulent halls.
whats_special: The legendary Garden Court restaurant features a stunning glass dome ceiling that's been a San Francisco landmark for over a century. This architectural marvel was meticulously restored after the 1906 earthquake and remains one of the most photographed dining rooms in America. The hotel also boasts the famous Maxfield Parrish painting "The Pied Piper" in the Pied Piper Bar, valued at millions.
pro_tip: Book afternoon tea in the Garden Court during golden hour (3-4 PM) when natural light streams through the glass dome, creating an almost ethereal dining experience that photographers dream of.
dont_miss: The hotel's prime location puts you steps from Union Square's luxury shopping and just blocks from the cable car turnaround. Take the historic elevator to explore the hotel's "ghost floor" - the mezzanine level where you can view the Garden Court from above and spot original 1909 architectural details that survived the rebuilding.
pros: Historic landmark property with stunning architecture and grandeur
Prime downtown San Francisco location near Union Square
Exceptional service standards as part of Marriott STARS Program
Elegant accommodations with luxury amenities and classic design
cons: Historic building may have smaller room configurations
